title: AI user code of conduct attestation
description: Attest that the issuer is committed to follow a particular code of conduct with respect to their personal use of AI. A public, self-issued declaration: it names no issuee, because the issuer is declaring something about itself.
$comment: Public by design, like bindkey: a declaration nobody can see does no work, so no privacy nonce is declared in either slot and heti mints none.

t.description: Message type. Optional; an ACDC JSON message without it is of type acm.

i.description: AID of the issuer making the declaration

rd.description: SAID of the registry whose TEL carries this credential's issuance and revocation. Required: a public commitment that cannot be withdrawn is worse than none, because it outlives the issuer's willingness to stand behind it.

dt.description: When the issuer made this declaration, as an ISO-8601 datetime

validFrom.description: When the commitment takes effect, as an ISO-8601 datetime. Absent means it takes effect on issuance.

validUntil.description: When the commitment stops, as an ISO-8601 datetime. Absent means the issuer set no horizon, so it stands until revoked — never that it is perpetual.

coc.description: The code of conduct the issuer commits to. SHOULD hold the SAID of a document published elsewhere, or HTML encoded as a data URL. MAY hold an ordinary URL, in which case the issuer commits to whatever is published there rather than to specific content — see the referencedCodeMayChange rule.

oneOf.const: The issuer declares an intention to abide by the named code of conduct. This credential is not evidence that the issuer has abided by it, and a verifier MUST NOT read compliance, audit or enforcement into a declaration of intent.

l.const: The issuer declares an intention to abide by the named code of conduct. This credential is not evidence that the issuer has abided by it, and a verifier MUST NOT read compliance, audit or enforcement into a declaration of intent.

oneOf.const: Where coc holds an ordinary URL rather than a SAID or a data URL, the issuer commits to whatever is published at that location, which can change after issuance. A verifier relying on such a declaration MUST fetch the code of conduct and judge it for itself, and MUST NOT assume the content it sees is the content the issuer saw.

l.const: Where coc holds an ordinary URL rather than a SAID or a data URL, the issuer commits to whatever is published at that location, which can change after issuance. A verifier relying on such a declaration MUST fetch the code of conduct and judge it for itself, and MUST NOT assume the content it sees is the content the issuer saw.

oneOf.const: This is a self-issued public declaration, not a credential granted by a third party. It carries no vetting, and whatever weight it has comes from the issuer being publicly accountable for having made it.
